title: BCG’s Intelligent Cities Index 2026
gist: BCG's inaugural Intelligent Cities Index scores 61 cities across 39 countries on 35 indicators and finds London, Dubai, New York City, Washington, and Amsterdam leading, with no city topping every domain. The core finding is that embedding AI into core municipal services correlates with better resident outcomes, and that adoption is now the easy part — cities hit a ceiling unless soft enablers (talent, venture capital, FDI) match hard enablers (data, infrastructure, IoT).

themes.theme: Index construction and the leadership tier

insights.claim: BCG's inaugural Intelligent Cities Index benchmarks 61 cities across 39 countries using 35 indicators grouped into five domains (outcomes, strategy, adoption, ways of working, enablers) and 14 dimensions, with six core indicators normalized against benchmarks or the 75th percentile and consolidated into four maturity tiers.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: A new, city-level scoring rubric that vendors of urban AI, IoT, and e-government platforms can use to target which municipalities have budget, strategy, and governance readiness rather than just headline GDP.

insights.claim: London, Dubai, New York City, Washington, and Amsterdam are the only cities rated at leading maturity, each leading in two or more of the five domains, yet no single city leads every domain.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Even the top-ranked municipal markets have unfilled capability gaps, meaning addressable procurement opportunities exist in the wealthiest cities, not only in laggards.
insights.quote: The five leading cities are London, Dubai, New York City, Washington, and Amsterdam. All five show leading maturity across two or more of the five domains.
insights.locator: The five leading cities are London, Dubai

themes.theme: AI embedded in core services as the outcome driver

insights.claim: Roughly one-third of the 61 indexed cities lead in AI adoption, and these cities simultaneously post the highest number of deployed use cases and the highest quality-of-life scores, making AI integration into daily city operations the strongest observed correlate of resident outcomes.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Public-sector AI deployment is moving from pilot to core-operations budget lines in a third of major global cities — a demand signal for government AI service providers.
insights.quote: A striking pattern stands out: cities that are embedding AI into core services are delivering faster, better resident outcomes.
insights.locator: AI Is a Key Foundation of the Intelligent City

insights.claim: Progress in intelligent-city maturity is explicitly non-linear: a city starting from a low base of AI use cases can still drive resident outcomes by expanding deployment, as shown by the AI-driven challengers and AI-light performers cohorts.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Undermines the assumption that only rich, already-digitized cities are viable markets; late-starting municipalities can leapfrog and represent an under-served buyer segment.
insights.quote: Yet the positioning of AI-driven challengers and AI-light performers suggests that progress is not linear; a city can drive resident outcomes by expanding AI deployment even if it starts with a lower number of use cases.
insights.locator: Yet the positioning of AI-driven challengers

insights.claim: Frequency of GenAI tool use among residents maps directly onto positive sentiment about AI's future role: the highest-use cohort, labeled AI enthusiasts, also registers the highest sentiment, while pragmatic power users outscore cautious users.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Consumer AI usage is self-reinforcing rather than novelty-driven — supportive of durable engagement and monetization assumptions for GenAI consumer products.
insights.quote: residents who have the highest use—AI enthusiasts—also have the highest sentiment
insights.locator: AI Adoption, User Optimism, and the Virtuous Circle of AI Value

insights.claim: Cities across Africa, Asia, and the Middle East report the strongest AI enthusiasm and adoption among residents, outpacing the sentiment baseline in other geographies.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Emerging-market urban populations, not Western ones, are the sentiment leaders for AI — relevant to where consumer AI adoption curves steepen fastest.
insights.quote: Several geographies especially share this outlook, with cities throughout Africa, Asia, and the Middle East reporting strong enthusiasm and adoption.
insights.locator: Several geographies especially share this outlook

insights.claim: Smart city app usage frequency and resident satisfaction move together — London and Dubai score high on both, while satisfaction is quite low in cities with below-average usage frequency — and usage plus satisfaction skew toward younger cities where more than half the population is under 35.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Demographics are a screening variable for civic-tech demand: young-population cities are the higher-conversion market for municipal app platforms.
insights.quote: Several cities where more than half of the population is under age 35 fall in the standout cohort.
insights.locator: Our study finds that use and satisfaction tend to be higher in younger cities

themes.theme: Hard enablers get you partway; soft enablers set the ceiling

insights.claim: 37 of the 61 indexed cities, including Dublin, have achieved a balance between hard enablers (data, tech, infrastructure) and soft enablers (talent, funding), and this balance is the defining trait of the most mature cities.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Roughly 60% of major cities clear the balance bar, so differentiation among vendors and investors shifts to the talent and capital side rather than hardware.
insights.quote: In all, 37 cities have found this balance, including Dublin.
insights.locator: A balance of hard and soft enablers drives a city forward

insights.claim: Infrastructure strength alone caps a city's ceiling — Sydney earns only accelerating maturity despite strength in infrastructure and living labs, because reaching leading maturity requires talent development plus funding ecosystems including venture capital and foreign direct investment.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Capital flows (VC and FDI) are treated as a hard prerequisite for urban tech maturity — city rankings become a proxy read on where startup funding ecosystems are actually deep.
insights.quote: But technology isn’t enough if a city wants to reach the highest levels of maturity.
insights.locator: A story forms: a city can build a strong infrastructure foundation

insights.claim: Four of the Index's top cities score highest in both economic opportunities and ecosystem-and-funding assessments, linking entrepreneurship and innovation ecosystem strength directly to economic outcomes at the top of the ranking — but the relationship breaks down for less mature cities, where weak ecosystems produce highly uneven rather than uniformly poor outcomes.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Ecosystem strength is a reliable signal only in the top tier; screening mid-tier cities on ecosystem metrics alone will produce false negatives.
insights.quote: Weaker ecosystems do not guarantee poorer economic outcomes but instead show highly uneven performance.
insights.locator: It’s harder to find clear patterns among less mature cities

themes.theme: Domain-level winners and the adoption ceiling

insights.claim: Adoption posted the highest overall scores of any of the five domains, with progress spanning from the top five cities down to Lagos, showing that cities can build resident optimism through AI and apps even without strong infrastructure or funding.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Adoption is commoditized and no longer a differentiator — the scarce inputs are governance and funding, which is where value accrues.
insights.quote: Adoption showed the highest overall scores of any domain in the Index.
insights.locator: Adoption. The Index assessed adoption of smart city apps

insights.claim: Adoption is broadly achieved but frequently capped, with many cities unable to scale intelligent-city or AI use cases beyond a limit because enablers and ways of working are not in place.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Expect pilot-to-scale attrition in public-sector AI: revenue from municipal AI contracts may plateau well below headline use-case counts.
insights.quote: However, while adoption is broadly achieved, it is often capped; many cities can push intelligent city or AI use cases only so far.
insights.locator: However, while adoption is broadly achieved

insights.claim: Domain leadership is dispersed across cities with very different overall maturity: London leads outcomes, Madrid leads strategy, Dubai leads adoption alongside Mumbai, Manchester, and Boston, Berlin leads ways of working via a dedicated smart city unit inside its business development agency, and Amsterdam leads enablers with a startup density unusual for a sub-million-resident city plus the top score for living labs.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Different cities are reference customers for different capability sales motions — strategy consulting into Madrid, governance and PPP into Berlin, testbed and startup partnering into Amsterdam.
insights.quote: Amsterdam leads this domain with a robust community of startups for a city of under a million residents; many larger cities count far fewer startups.
insights.locator: Enablers. One of the study’s recurring takeaways

insights.claim: Institutional AI readiness correlates with the number of AI-enabled use cases deployed, but readiness alone does not determine results: some high-readiness cities are slow to convert capability into action while several modest-readiness cities drive meaningful deployment.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Readiness scores are a weak predictor of actual procurement — track deployed use-case counts and PPP formation instead.
insights.quote: Some high-readiness cities still move slower in turning capability into action, while several cities with modest readiness manage to drive meaningful deployment.
insights.locator: Ways of Working. The Index analyzed each city’s implementation of governance

themes.theme: Two viable pathways: balanced builders vs focused specialists

insights.claim: There is no single route to intelligent-city maturity: balanced builders reach at least accelerating scores across all capability domains with leading maturity on two or more, while focused specialists climb the ranks by doubling down on one or two domains such as strategy, ways of working, or enablers.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Segmentation model for anyone selling into or investing around municipal digitalization: balanced builders buy broad platforms, focused specialists buy point solutions in their chosen domain.
insights.locator: Choose the Right Pathway to Success

insights.claim: The prescribed roadmap sequences four moves — clarify long-term strategic priorities to concentrate AI and digital investment where residents actually engage government and the economy, tighten governance with accountable owners and partnerships, scale adoption by expanding proven apps and AI solutions, and build enablers across data platforms, infrastructure, talent, and ecosystem.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Signals where municipal spend is directed next: proven-app expansion and data-platform upgrades rather than greenfield pilots.
insights.locator: A roadmap lays out the important steps toward stronger outcomes
